source_caption:
🎬 Big Trouble (2002)

Big Trouble follows a group of strangers in Miami whose lives unexpectedly become intertwined through a series of chaotic misunderstandings and bizarre circumstances. Eliot Arnold, a struggling advertising executive and divorced father, becomes involved with Anna Herk, an unhappy woman married to a corrupt businessman. Meanwhile, two professional hitmen, incompetent criminals, police officers, and a mysterious homeless man find themselves caught up in an increasingly ridiculous situation involving a dangerous suitcase. As their separate stories collide, ordinary encounters quickly escalate into outrageous adventures filled with confusion, unexpected twists, and hilarious confrontations. Starring Tim Allen, Rene Russo, Stanley Tucci, and Ben Foster, the film delivers fast-paced comedy, eccentric characters, and entertaining storytelling while exploring crime, relationships, coincidence, and the unpredictable consequences of being in the wrong place at the wrong time.

🎭 Genre: Comedy • Crime • Thriller

⭐ IMDb: 6.4/10

⏱️ Runtime: 1h 25m • PG-13

🎥 Director: Barry Sonnenfeld

📚 Based On: The 1999 novel Big Trouble by Dave Barry.

📺 Where to Watch: Check Amazon Prime Video and Apple TV for current streaming, rental, or purchase availability in the United States.

source_details.synopsis: Big Trouble is a 2002 American black comedy film based on the novel Big Trouble by Dave Barry. It was directed by Barry Sonnenfeld and featured a large cast including Tim Allen and Rene Russo with Dennis Farina, Zooey Deschanel, Sofia Vergara, in her film debut, and Jason Lee in supporting roles. Like much of Dave Barry's fiction, it follows a diverse group of people through a series of extremely strange and humorous situations against the backdrop of Miami. Big Trouble was released by Buena Vista Pictures Distribution on April 5, 2002. The film was a box-office bomb as it grossed $8.5 million against a $40 million budget, and received mixed critical reception.
